Robot Tutorial native Windows verification -- 2026-09-29
======================================================

Scope
-----
Executed the reader-facing PowerShell blocks in windows.md from Chapter 2
through Appendix C, including MSBuild discovery, Chapter 5 helper assembly,
both Chapter 5 module builds, and the optional XML/image Copy-Item commands.
Chapter 1 had already been checked by the maintainer; its working copy was
preserved. This check used the existing TORCS development installation.

Platform: Windows, Visual Studio 2022 Professional, v143, Release/x64.
MSBuild: 17.14.60; compiler: MSVC 14.44.35207; language: C++14.
All nine module builds succeeded with zero warnings and zero errors.
No tutorial source/project/documentation correction was needed.

Native execution
----------------
Ran the freshly installed, uninstrumented DLLs through runtime/wtorcs.exe -r,
with runtime as the working directory, simuv2 and g-track-1. Every invocation
returned zero. Each case used a unique race configuration filename and a
previously nonexistent results directory. Checked fresh result XML for the
expected module/index entries and completed laps; copied results into evidence.

Chapter 2 includes its supplied deliberate starting mistake. The pace driver
was lapped in the mixed race. Chapter 6's demonstration used the documented
DEMONSTRATION_STOP=true edit and a native incremental rebuild. Afterwards,
restored false and rebuilt/reinstalled the default checkpoint.

Deployment and downloads
------------------------
Verified installed XML/RGB/artwork-notice files against their working sources.
Removed those generated runtime assets and reran the normal build commands:
all were restored. Appendix A/B/C required no C++ compilation or relinking
and still executed InstallTutorial, including C's index 1 and 2 folders.
Asset counts: Chapter 6: 1; Appendix A: 3; B: 6; C: 11.
Compared every file in tutorial6.zip, tutoriala.zip, tutorialb.zip and
tutorialc.zip with the tested working sources (COPYING against root COPYING).
All matched byte-for-byte: 24, 28, 34 and 45 archive files respectively.

Evidence and limits
-------------------
Local evidence directory:
C:\Users\berni\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\tutorial-windows-_v1jgcv6

report.json and numbered .ps1/.log files: executed documentation blocks/builds.
races.json: eleven baseline race cases, DLL/executable/physics/config hashes,
exit codes and result rows. races-ch6-demo.json: demonstration race evidence.
*-race.log, *-result.xml and race configuration XML: fresh runtime evidence.
deployment.json and *-redeploy.log: asset/archive and incremental build checks.
Scratch runners are in the parent opencode directory:
verify_tutorial_windows.py, run_tutorial_windows.py,
check_tutorial_deployment.py.

This establishes native Release/x64 build, installation and headless execution.
It does not establish GUI appearance, in-menu unload/reload, Debug/Win32,
or exhaustive driving-experiment/performance correctness. Linux verification
was outside this run. Existing user edits were preserved. The new reader
working copies remain in src/drivers/tutorial2..6 and tutoriala..c, with their
modules/assets installed in runtime/drivers for subsequent manual use.

Maintained verification runner -- 2026-09-29
------------------------------------------
The scratch checks above have been consolidated into
test/robot_tutorial/check_windows.py. See that directory's README for the
command, prerequisites, platform boundary and profile/result isolation.
This runner builds in a private tree rather than the reader working copies.
It shares archive/reporting helpers and race XML/entry/result helpers with
the existing Linux checks, and reuses supported scenarios.json definitions.

Full Release/x64 run passed: nine DLL builds, zero warnings/errors, archive
and deployment checks, and eleven native race cases (the separate Chapter 5
solo smoke case from the initial session is redundant with the pace case).
Evidence: C:\Users\berni\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\win-sz_g5rb_

test_verification.py: all ten portable infrastructure tests passed, including
failure/timeout reporting and negative result checks. The refactored race XML
was also compared with the previous Linux generator: all 29 existing scenario
configurations remained byte-identical. Verified that all three Linux native
execution entry points reject Windows before launching native tools.
No native Linux build/race was rerun during this Windows maintenance session.
